chapter: Writing, Oklahoma roots and the origins of bebop
title: Bird's melodic ways and influence
summary: Bird fit melodies on any changes and educated more people than any musician.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: How about the practice of...? Was Bird the first one to do this, that you remember, of mixing patterns? Like with 'Scrapple From The Apple,' taking 'Honeysuckle Rose' and putting a 'I Got Rhythm' bridge to it.
No. I think that all those tunes came about

because they used to play them down on the street, on 52nd Street. And Bird just had nice little melodies for... Anything that he wanted to put something on something, he'd just fit it on there, because he knew what he was doing. He was really brilliant when it comes to that.
Well, he would come up with... Quoting, of course, is another thing that went back before that.
And Tatum was one of the masters at doing that.
But it seemed Bird would come up out of left field with some tune in the middle of another tune.

Yeah. Well, Bird had a very melodic way of putting things, you know. The way he played his horn, the way he would play a song, he had his own of doing it that nobody else was playing like that. When I first heard him, he sounded so different, I had never heard nobody play like that, and I had worked...you know, I came to work with Hawk and all of the other big names that was out here, like Ben Webster and all this... But Bird, pshew, I don't know where he come from, all of a sudden, out of nowhere. Like the song says, 'Out of No Where.'
Do you think he influenced the whole...
The idea of phrasing, the way to get from one note to the next -- he seemed to have his own way of doing that.

Everything. Everything. Anything that he wanted to do, he had it all mapped out. I don't know nobody who played like Bird -- or thought like Bird. Especially at that time. They got some guys out here now who can run a lot of notes. But they don't really have much to say about what the situation is. Bird just said about everything. He talked about everything. And knew about everything! He told me about some things I didn't really believe anybody knew that much knowledge about certain things that was going on. But Bird would talk to you and tell you about it. In fact, I think he educated more people than any one musician I know.
